newsitem.title: ITALY: Romanian NATO bid aided by Albania force - Italy.
newsitem.headline: Romanian NATO bid aided by Albania force - Italy.

text.p: Italy said on Thursday that Romania's bid to be included in the first wave of new entrants to NATO and join the European Union had been aided by its participation in a multinational security force in Albania.

"Italy completely supports Romania to be part of the EU and NATO which will be decided not any later than July," Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said after meeting his Romanian counterpart Adrian Severin for talks in Rome.

Dini said the contribution of Romanian soldiers to an Italian-led multinational force, which left for Albania this week to protect the distribution of aid, had given Bucharest a boost in seeking entry to the two organisations.

"We thank Romania for its important contribution to the multinational force...which is a European and indirectly a NATO exercise," Dini told reporters. Asked whether this would help Romania's case, Dini said: "absolutely".
Severin is on a four-day visit to Italy after which he will travel to the United States to push Romanian entry to NATO.

Neither the United States nor Germany has offered overt backing for Romania's drive to be invited to join the Western military alliance when a decision is made on expansion into former communist eastern Europe at a summit in Madrid in July.
Romania, along with Slovenia, whose application Italy also supports, remain long-shots behind Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
